goal: See that the steepness of the line, not its height, tells you the speed at a moment.
brief: A distance-time graph: x-axis is Time (0 to 10 seconds), y-axis is Distance (0 to 100 meters). A draggable point sits on a bent-line path. A slider changes the steepness of the second segment of the path, and the picture shows the speed readout update live.

controls.label: Steepness of segment 2
controls.effect: Tilts the second part of the line up or down, making it steeper or flatter, and the speed readout changes to match.

controls.label: Time position
controls.effect: Moves a marker dot along the path so you can see distance and current steepness at that exact moment.

controls.label: Show tangent line
controls.effect: Draws the touching line at the marker's position so you can see the local steepness even on a curved path.

try_this: Make segment 2 flat and watch the speed readout drop to zero.
Make segment 2 very steep and see the speed number jump up.
Turn on the tangent line and slide the marker along a curve to watch the speed change smoothly.
